blocks.raw: # Core Concepts
blocks.text: Core Concepts

blocks.raw: Creating an effective loyalty promotion involves defining a clear business objective, identifying the target audience, and establishing precise earning criteria to deliver relevant rewards while maintaining control through participation and reward limits.
blocks.text: Creating an effective loyalty promotion involves defining a clear business objective, identifying the target audience, and establishing precise earning criteria to deliver relevant rewards while maintaining control through participation and reward limits.

blocks.raw: # Objective
blocks.text: Objective

blocks.raw: A promotion's objective is its primary business goal, such as driving a specific member behavior or distributing a direct reward. This objective is defined by selecting a promotion type, which determines how a member is eligible for and receives the loyalty promotion benefits.
blocks.text: A promotion's objective is its primary business goal, such as driving a specific member behavior or distributing a direct reward. This objective is defined by selecting a promotion type, which determines how a member is eligible for and receives the loyalty promotion benefits.

blocks.raw: # Eligibility
blocks.text: Eligibility

blocks.raw: Eligibility defines who can participate in the promotion. This is managed through a two-step process: enrolment determines the target audience, while the optional opt-in requires members to consciously signal their interest.
blocks.text: Eligibility defines who can participate in the promotion. This is managed through a two-step process: enrolment determines the target audience, while the optional opt-in requires members to consciously signal their interest.

blocks.raw: **Enrolment**: This is the first step that defines the broad audience for the promotion. You can target all members of your loyalty program or target specific members based on predefined audience groups, their completion of a qualifying activity, or an external trigger via the enrol API call.

blocks.raw:
> 📘 Note:
>
> If your promotion includes an opt-in step and your enrolment is set to **all members** (including non-loyalty members), the opt-in action will fail for non-loyalty members because they cannot be enrolled in a loyalty program. This failure halts all further event processing for that member — including any communication actions such as emails configured in the same event flow. To avoid this, set the enrolment criteria to **loyalty members only** so that non-loyalty members are excluded from the promotion and their events continue to be processed normally.

blocks.raw: # **Duration**
blocks.text: Duration

blocks.raw: The duration defines the specific timeframe during which a promotion is active. Here, you can define the start and end dates and times for the loyalty promotion. You can also define the duration timezone.
blocks.text: The duration defines the specific timeframe during which a promotion is active. Here, you can define the start and end dates and times for the loyalty promotion. You can also define the duration timezone.

blocks.raw:
* **[Timezone Management](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/timezone-management):** Promotions operate in a specified timezone to ensure accuracy across different regions. All date and time configurations are handled in the **ISO 8601 standard**, which includes a timezone offset. Each promotion is also tagged with a timezone name, for example,`Asia/New Delhi` to maintain a clear record of its intended operational timezone.
* **Default Timing:** If you select a start and end date without specifying a time, the promotion will run for the full duration of those days, defaulting to a start time of **00:00** and an end time of **23:59** in the chosen timezone.

blocks.raw: # Earning criteria
blocks.text: Earning criteria

blocks.raw: Earning criteria define the specific behaviors required to earn a loyalty promotion's reward. This involves selecting an **activity type** to structure the goal, such as a one-time single action or a cumulative milestone, identifying the **member action** to track, such as making a transaction, and applying **qualifying conditions** to ensure rewards are granted only for exact behaviors.

This involves selecting an activity type to structure the goal, such as a one-time single action or a cumulative milestone, identifying the member action to track, such as making a transaction, and applying qualifying conditions to ensure rewards are granted only for exact behaviors.

blocks.raw: ## Member activities
blocks.text: Member activities

blocks.raw: Activities define the core logic of a loyalty promotion's earning criteria. They determine how a member's actions result in rewards and serve as the foundation for driving specific behaviors, such as repeat purchases or increased engagement.
blocks.text: Activities define the core logic of a loyalty promotion's earning criteria. They determine how a member's actions result in rewards and serve as the foundation for driving specific behaviors, such as repeat purchases or increased engagement.

blocks.raw: A loyalty promotion activity can be one of three types:
blocks.text: A loyalty promotion activity can be one of three types:

blocks.raw:
* **Single:** Rewards a one-time action, such as purchasing a specific featured product.
* **Milestone:** Rewards a cumulative target reached over time, such as spending a total of $200 across multiple transactions.
* **Streak:** Rewards consistent, consecutive behavior, such as making a transaction once a week for three consecutive weeks.

blocks.raw: ### Cycles in milestone-based promotions
blocks.text: Cycles in milestone-based promotions

blocks.raw: Cycles are the mechanism that transforms a single, one-time milestone into a recurring challenge. They encourage consistent, repeated member behavior by defining a reset period for a goal. Without cycles, a milestone like "Spend $100" is a goal a member achieves only once. With a monthly cycle, it becomes an ongoing challenge: "Spend $100 each month to earn a reward."
blocks.text: Cycles are the mechanism that transforms a single, one-time milestone into a recurring challenge. They encourage consistent, repeated member behavior by defining a reset period for a goal. Without cycles, a milestone like "Spend $100" is a goal a member achieves only once. With a monthly cycle, it becomes an ongoing challenge: "Spend $100 each month to earn a reward."

blocks.raw: The core of a cycle is its reset period. This defines the time window (such as daily, weekly, or monthly) during which a member's progress is tracked. At the end of each period, their progress resets to zero, and they must restart the challenge. Also, the cycle start date determines when the challenge begins for a member. It can be configured to start uniformly for all participants (for example, on the promotion start date) or to begin personally for each member only when they perform their first qualifying activity.

blocks.raw: ## Member actions
blocks.text: Member actions

blocks.raw: The member action is a specific event or behavior that is the trigger for a promotion's earning criteria. This selection is a key part of the rule, defining the primary member interaction to monitor. It determines the nature of the promotion, whether it rewards a transactional behavior like making a purchase, an engagement activity like updating a profile, a loyalty interaction such as redeeming points, or any other custom behavioral event. Refer to the document on [Member Actions](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/loyalty-promotions-member-actions) for more details.

blocks.raw: ## Qualifying conditions and attributes
blocks.text: Qualifying conditions and attributes

blocks.raw: Qualifying conditions are the specific rules that an activity must meet to be considered valid for a loyalty promotion. While an activity defines a general member action, such as "making a transaction", qualifying conditions provide the necessary precision. This is achieved by adding criteria based on specific attributes related to the member, user groups, purchase details, payment modes, or other event data. By using these conditions, you can ensure that rewards are granted only for the exact behaviors you intend to target. Refer to the document on [Qualifying Conditions and Attributes](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/loyalty-promotions-qualifying-conditions) for more details.

blocks.raw: # **Incentives**
blocks.text: Incentives

blocks.raw: An incentive is what a member receives upon completing a qualifying action. These are configured as brand actions. Rewards can range from issuing loyalty points and alternate currencies to managing a member's tier status. The configuration allows for precise control over the reward value, its expiry, and the timing of its issuance.

blocks.raw: # **Communication**
blocks.text: Communication

blocks.raw: Communications can be configured to automatically trigger at key moments in the member's promotion journey. This allows you to send targeted messages, such as via email or SMS, to keep members informed and engaged. Messages can be sent upon successful enrolment, successful opt-in, or as part of a reward action itself. You can send a communication to members using the [Send Communication](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/loyalty-promotions-actions#send-communication) action or when configuring an action that supports communications.

blocks.raw: # **Limits**
blocks.text: Limits

blocks.raw: Participation and reward limits are essential controls that set the boundaries for a loyalty promotion, ensuring it remains effective and financially viable. They are divided into two main categories: those that manage member participation and those that limit the rewards.
blocks.text: Participation and reward limits are essential controls that set the boundaries for a loyalty promotion, ensuring it remains effective and financially viable. They are divided into two main categories: those that manage member participation and those that limit the rewards.

blocks.raw: Participation limits govern the promotion's lifecycle by defining who is eligible to join, how many times they can enrol, and the total number of participants allowed. In contrast, reward limits control the benefits themselves, limiting the total points a member can earn or the number of times a qualifying activity can be rewarded. Together, these limits are crucial for managing the promotion's budget, preventing reward abuse, and strategically creating a sense of exclusivity or urgency. Refer to the document on [Loyalty Promotion Limits](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/loyalty-promotions-limits) for more details.
